meta.title: WoW Forever Warrior spell ranks, every level 1-60

status_legend.forever: Forever client data (build 1.60.1.70862) as carried by wowsims-forever

source.records: sim/core/spelldata/spells_auto_gen.go (wowsims's generator bakes in tools/database/overrides; any override comment is copied to the rank's wowsims_overrides: those fields are wowsims's in-game measurements, not client rows)
source.vanilla: cmangos classic-db spell_template (1.12) for vanilla_* fields, npc_trainer_template 11 + npc_trainer rows of class 1 trainers for vanilla_trainer (teach spell -> learned spell through effect 36 LEARN_SPELL)

formulas.value_at_level: BasePoints + PPL * clamp(min(L, scaling_max_level) - scaling_base_level, 0); scaling_max_level 0 = no cap. Computed in float32 as wowsims Effect.AverageAt. Damage/heal amounts keep the fraction; every other amount is floored.
formulas.cost: cost.mana flat; cost.pct_base_mana = pct of base mana (base_mana table in <class>_levels.json); cost.rage in rage (row value / 10); cost.energy; cost.combo_points_min = the finisher needs at least that many; cost.health (Life Tap row has none: wowsims spends amount + Spirit).
formulas.learn_level: SpellLevels.SpellLevel of the rank (client). learned_from.vanilla_trainer gives the vanilla 1.12 trainer level and cost for comparison. 2 Nov notes: training every class ability 1-60 costs 206-207 gold in Forever, so vanilla costs are not Forever costs.
formulas.vanilla_compare: vanilla.changes_vs_vanilla compares learn level, flat cost, cooldowns and each effect's amount at the learn level (vanilla BasePoints+1 .. BasePoints+DieSides, Forever tooltip range) with the 1.12 row of the same id. A difference of 1 point or less is ignored. Cast times and durations are not compared (the 1.12 rows store index ids into tables not in the local data).
formulas.required_stance_mask: client StanceMask bit field (1 << (form id - 1)); e.g. warrior Battle 17, Defensive 18, Berserker 19; druid Cat 1, Bear 5, Dire Bear 8, Moonkin 31.

coefficient_penalties.finding: Neither wowsims-forever nor mythicsim-forever-engine applies the vanilla sub-20 penalty (1 - (20 - spellLevel)*0.0375) or a downrank coefficient penalty. Ranks learned below 20 carry sp_coef_if_vanilla_sub20_penalty so a sim can switch the vanilla rule on.
coefficient_penalties.forever_notes: kami-labs summary of the 2 Nov 2026 notes: the low-rank penalty was removed from several chance-based talents and stays on Arcane Concentration, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost (proc less often when the rank was learned more than 12 levels below the caster). Nothing in the notes speaks to damage/heal coefficients of low ranks.

forever_class_notes: Rage (deep dive 1 Oct 2026, Warcraft Tavern summary): fully normalized on weapon speed; crits +75% rage (the client 'Rule of Rage' row and wowsims logs say +100%: client wins); rage from damage taken ignores armor. See warrior_levels.json meta.resources.
New baseline: Victory Rush (20). Thunder Clap 6 s cooldown and AP scaling, usable in Defensive Stance. Recklessness/Retaliation/Shield Wall cooldowns split; Retaliation and Shield Wall 15 min.
4 Nov notes: Defensive Stance threat 80% (was 30%); Slam cooldown 15 s.
notes_sources: Warcraft Tavern summaries of Blizzard's Forever class deep dives: Priest & Warrior (1 Oct 2026, Blizzard news 24301514), Mage & Shaman (7 Oct, 24302097), Rogue & Warlock (7 Oct, 24310968); 'All Changes to Paladins' (21 Sep 2026); 'WoW Forever Pre-Launch Class Changes & Bug Fixes' (4 Nov 2026, from Kaivax's Beta Development Notes updated 2 Nov).
Blizzard news 'World of Warcraft: Forever Class Deep Dives - Hunter and Druid' (news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24301515).
kami-labs 'WoW Forever November 2 patch: 223 changes before launch' (datamined items marked).
The Blizzard forum dev-notes thread itself could not be fetched here (needs approval); its content is taken from the summaries above.
Where a note and a client row disagree, the row wins; the row values are the ones in ranks[].

notes: Deep dive (Warcraft Tavern 1 Oct 2026): Battle Shout's attack power was reduced and Improved Battle Shout is 'baked in'. Rank 7 (25289) is a book rank (Manual of Battle Shout VII). Values per level come from the row (points_per_level up to max_level).

wowsims_code_notes.comment: How close to running out the warrior's own shout has to be before recasting it is worth a global. Rank 6 is the top rank the trainer teaches; Rank 7 comes from Manual of Battle Shout VII. A warrior that shouts builds its own copy. One that never shouts gets the isPlayer=false constructor, whose aura is the raid's external copy, and the raid's Battle Shout state sets what that copy is worth. Three pieces of Battlegear of Wrath add a flat 30 to the shout. HasBsT2 is set by the user or by the set worn at the start. The set is worth the 30 on the shout this warrior makes, so it raises what that copy applies and what the cast is worth to the category together. The class option decides which rank's own copy the character sheet shows, as the rank the rotation picks is unknown when the sheet is built. The rotation alone decides the rank cast. The raid's Battle Shout registers the external copy of its rank before this runs, and that copy keeps the build phase it was registered with. Booming Voice widens the radius and lowers the cost only, so the aura takes no talent points. What holds the Battle Shout category decides whether shouting is worth a global. Nothing there and the cast puts the buff up. This rank's own copy there and the cast only refreshes it, which is worth a global once it is about to run out. Anything else has to be outbid first, as a warrior without the set would otherwise keep recasting a shout the category turns away while a stronger external one is up. effects.weapon_effect: flat damage added to a weapon hit

wowsims_code_notes.comment: The proc opens Overpower's window as a dodge would, for the window's own duration, and the cast consumes it. The tooltip's $s1 names an effect, so the row's own ProcChanceEffectN reads the rate ladder. Main-hand white swings, extra attacks included, and the on-next-swing Heroic Strike and Cleave proc it on a target with the warrior's Rend; the row's melee-ability bit would also admit the instant specials, which in game do not proc it.

The three branches share A_DUMMY and misc 0, so each is named by its effect index. The aura is up while either hand holds an axe or a polearm, and its crit reaches the attacks made with one. The aura is up while either hand holds a one- or two-handed mace or a staff, and its armor ignore reaches every attack. A mace in each hand ignores the share once. 1290261 states no proc flags at all, so the row decodes to a listener that hears nothing: the shape, the mask and the rate's effect are all the caller's. Measured in game, Sweeping Strikes' hits never roll it, and Whirlwind and Cleave roll it once a cast however many targets they land on. Which target's hit takes that roll is not measured; here the first landed one does, since a hit that is avoided never reaches the condition. A Windfury Totem swing's proc brings no extra swing; only the totem's swing is measured, so swings other procs gra

12966 supplies the duration and the three charges. The haste is the talent's 10% per point, which 12319 reads as "Increases your melee attack speed by $m1% for your next $12966n swings"; the buff row's flat 30% does not apply. The proc shape with no roll: 12319 states its rate as "always" and the crit is the condition, which this handler reads off the result because the same listener hears every melee result. Every white swing uses a charge whatever its outcome, and a Heroic Strike or Cleave uses one only when it misses. The row's mask reaches ranged and spell hits too; the tooltip says a melee critical strike, so the mask stays the caller's.  TODO: Ingame test needed: the Cleave miss follows the measured Heroic Strike miss; no log holds a missed Cleave yet.

wowsims_code_notes.comment: Victorious State hears the killing blow and casts Victorious, which Victory Rush needs and spends. The kill roll stands for the game's experience or honor check, so an add counts like any enemy. The attack deals its heal itself, so both show on one row. The heal makes healing threat as any heal does: half the health it restores, times the stance, split between the enemies in combat. Whether healing done and taken modifiers change it is not measured, so it restores the row's share of maximum health with none of them. It skips the healing calculation, which would add the attack's damage modifiers, and counts no second hit.
